change: Range boundaries come from the index. The builder takes RANGE_SIZE (widest range, any value 1..32768) and an optional POSTINGS_CAP; with a cap, a range also closes before its total postings would exceed it. The kernel reads range_start instead of computing range*W.
justification_from_profile: 20261114-cuda5-profile-01: the busiest range ran a median 185 decode tiles per query against a mean of 47, and 245 ranges needed 1.07 waves of about 230 resident blocks.
behaviour_deltas_vs_variant_4: Uniform indexes (cap 0) are byte-identical to variant 3/4 files and produce the same ranges; the kernel reads two boundary words per block instead of multiplying.
Capped indexes use file version GSPRBP02 with flag 1, the cap and ranges+1 boundaries (4 bytes each); block widths follow each range's own extent.
The builder report prints range count, narrowest/widest range and largest/mean postings per range for wave planning.
Per-range original-ID ranks are built from the stored boundaries.
review_before_running: Greedy rule: a range takes at least one document, so a single document above the cap forms its own range; widths never exceed RANGE_SIZE; boundaries start at 0 and end at the document count.
Blocks are grouped by a document-to-range table, so positions/gaps are relative to the stored range start in builder, round-trip check, Python decoder and kernel alike.
Loader: uniform files rebuild the same boundaries and keep the old range-count check; capped files must have strictly increasing boundaries of width <= RANGE_SIZE.
Shared score memory is still sized by RANGE_SIZE, the widest range.

findings.issue: A fixture coverage assertion (some block longer than one warp) cannot hold under a 40-posting cap.
findings.fix: The assertion now applies to uniform ranges; capped runs assert that at least one range was narrowed. No scorer or builder change.

findings.issue: The cap balances total postings per range, a query-independent proxy. At 1M the uniform ranges already differ by only 1.31x in total postings (max 636,134, mean 484,488), while the profile's 4x imbalance is in a query's own postings.
findings.handling: Recorded as a limit; whether the cap helps is an empirical question for the sweep.

checks: Fixtures uniform and with --postings-cap 40 (independent Python copy of the greedy rule checks stored boundaries); version-1 fixtures still pass; 100K/1M x 500 queries x k=10/1000 on a cap-400,000 index (302 ranges at 1M, narrowest 938 documents) with zero mismatches.
validation_limits: Real-data checks of the capped layout use one cap value; other caps are covered by fixtures only until the sweep's own correctness runs.
